policy.summary: A row is published only when it states its pipeline, its benchmark set with n, its grader, and an artifact. Every proportion carries a 95% interval. Comparators are labeled by how they were scored: same grader in our run, independent validator, vendor self-reported, or as published; only same-grader values share a bar with ours. Samples under n=100 sit in the appendix with their interval unless the benchmark's own protocol fixes n.

tiers.A: Public per-item artifact and public harness. Anyone can re-grade every item.
tiers.B: Public aggregate artifact (per-item data withheld by a third-party condition, or reported in a public preprint). Anyone can check the aggregate and the method.
tiers.C: Internal artifact, public release pending. Reported for completeness; weight it accordingly.

comparator_bases.same_grader_self_run: The comparator model was run by us, in the same harness, scored by the same grader.
comparator_bases.independent_validator: Run by the independent validator (Airpixels Innovations LLP) on the same protocol.
comparator_bases.vendor_reported: Reported by the vendor on its own run. Same grader family at best; never the same run.
comparator_bases.literature: Taken from a paper or the benchmark author. Different run, possibly a different item set.

policy.production_note: Production routes each query by clinical stakes to one of three tiers: Asha Base (P2, one retrieval-grounded pass), Asha Mid (P5, three-model merge), Asha Apex (P6, multi-expert ensemble with a domain-specialist composer). Every row names the tier that was measured. Base carries most routine traffic; Apex carries high-stakes traffic.
policy.live_display: This page is the live display of DNAi benchmarking. Ceiling-ladder readouts on the 5090 are synced into the Professional row's Also measured list by scripts/site/sync_ceiling_results.py and the page is rebuilt and redeployed after each readout; the canonical register in the repository follows through a pull request, and /api/benchmarks/verify reports whether the two copies match.

benchmarks.notes: Every arm on the board, ours and the bare frontier models, went through one harness and three graders, so the ranking is like-for-like. On the September board (Asha arms on the 12 September build, Fable 5.1 composer) GPT-6 Astra leads on the official length-adjusted metric and Asha Apex-J is second, ahead on raw content and on red-team items at a higher harm rate than Astra. We publish the ordering as measured. Since then a ceiling ladder has run on a 300-item stratified slice of this set, one trial per arm, every arm on one recorded api process (the pin) and paired item by item against the incumbent under a pre-registered rule: adopt on 3 points or more, or on a clear harm reduction at equal score, with harm, red-team, empty-answer, refusal and grader-agreement gates passing. Round 1 (17 Sep) moved the composer to GPT-6 Astra. Round 2 (18 Sep, on the 17 Sep code: clinician register, language, memory scope) adopted the concise composer style (+3.6 length-adjusted, p=0.01, harm within gate); the guarded style, a dated PubMed evidence variant and the query-aware retriever each read inside the noise band against that incumbent, and asserting a clinician audience on this physician-written set regressed on red-team items. The Opus 5 composer arm is running. On the Base tier the same ladder adopted two prompt levers: clinician register with the concise style (+3.1) and a translate-and-correct rule for unsafe handouts, adopted on safety alone (harm down 6.7 points overall and 9.3 on red-team items at equal score). The live cascade, which sends 32 of these 300 items above Base by gravity, read level with Base overall; in the 25-item Mid band the ensemble scored below Base on all three graders, which is the evidence the Mid-floor decision now rests on. Slice results are exploratory by design and do not replace the board. When round 2 closes, the incumbent runs the full 525 items twice against bare GPT-6 Astra twice on the same pin and graders; that pre-freeze number is listed here when it lands. The code-freeze battery (22 to 25 September, Professional 525 x 2 for Base, Mid and Apex on the frozen build) produces the number of record and replaces this row. Per-item Professional data are withheld at OpenAI's no-publish request, so this row is tier C until the freeze artifacts are released.

benchmarks.lay_summary: The 525 questions a clinician asks in practice (dosing, differentials, management), graded against physician checklists. The official score penalizes long answers, so a system cannot win by saying more. Every system on this board was scored by the same grader in the same run, which is what makes the ranking fair. The rows under Also measured are one experiment at a time on the same 300 questions: each row names what changed, what it was compared with, and whether the change was adopted, left alone, or rejected under a rule written before the run. The current best configuration wraps our architecture around the leading model and asks it to answer briefly; it leads that bare model on these questions at the same rate of harmful statements.

benchmarks.notes: The backbone is held fixed and only the surrounding architecture varies, so the May 2026 gain is attributable to the architecture. Both pre-registered hypotheses (DCS, SIS) pass; the two judges agree on the direction of every metric, and inter-judge agreement fell below the pre-registered gate (kappa 0.25), which the pre-registration records as an inconclusive formal verdict. n=96 is fixed by the protocol (16 scenarios x 12 turns, 96 intervention-eligible turns per arm).
